solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Power line held in that?

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: the letter for line is held inside the word for that

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in 'yon hill'

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about where an electrical cable is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a tall tower is what holds a power line aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead electricity cables are strung between tall lattice towers, so the tower is what holds the line up.

clue.text: Drunk slept badly having quaffed a claret

indicators.note: drinking something takes it inside, so the scrambled letters surround a
the letters of slept are rearranged, done badly

parts.note: claret is red wine, so red stands for it

explanation.surface: A tipsy person slept poorly after drinking some Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the five letters into PLSTE, 'having quaffed' takes A inside it to make PLASTE; claret is simply red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for very intoxicated, like hammered or legless.

clue.text: Stick supporting middle of blue flower

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath
the inner letters of blue, dropping its ends

parts.note: to pin something is to stick or fasten it

explanation.surface: A cane propping up a blue bloom in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' gives LU, the inner letters of bLUe; 'supporting' puts PIN below it.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall spiky garden plant with pea-like blooms is an example of a flower.

clue.text: Feeding see, I write crosswords for chocolate!

indicators.note: the piece is fed into the word for see

parts.note: to note something is to see or observe it
a crossword compiler sets puzzles, so writing crosswords is setting

explanation.surface: A crossword setter boasts of being paid in sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword compilers are called setters because they set puzzles; 'Feeding' splits the word for see after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a chocolate made with hazelnuts, from the French for little nut.

clue.text: Great winger's successful long shot?

definitions.meaning: a great seabird with an enormous wingspan
in golf, a hole completed three under par, achievable only with very long successful shots

explanation.surface: A wide footballer pulls off a spectacular score from distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer, but it is a bird; the golf score of three under par is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The huge seabird is the largest-winged flier, and golfers use its name for a score three strokes under par.

clue.text: Drink having appeal in different forms, on reflection

indicators.note: a mirror reflection reverses things, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: sex appeal is called both IT and SA, two forms of the same word

explanation.surface: A drink that looks attractive in various shapes, when you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' gives two forms, IT and SA, both slang for sex appeal; 'on reflection' reverses the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: This sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy is an example of a drink.

clue.text: One moving to invest capital has billed companion?

indicators.note: to invest is to surround, as a besieging army invests a city

parts.note: one who budges is a mover, so a budger
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A financier putting money in has issued a bill to a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' looks financial but here means to surround, as a besieging army invests a city.
explanation.definitionFit: This small parrot, kept as a pet, has a beak, so it is a companion with a bill.

clue.text: Scrap suit in the end, its pockets black?

indicators.note: only the last letter of suit is used
to pocket is to take inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: read as the plural of it: two of them
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Throwing away an outfit whose pockets have turned dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' is read as the plural of IT, so ITIT, which 'pockets' B to give ITBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty morsel of food or a snippet of gossip is a small piece, or scrap.

clue.text: Cook not happy at first with cake knocked over in a row

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so the letters of not are rearranged
only the first letter of happy is used
the word for cake is turned over, in a down clue reading upwards

parts.note: a torte is a rich layered cake

explanation.surface: A baker in a bad mood keeps toppling cakes, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges NOT into ONT; 'knocked over' reverses TORTE to ETROT.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom means consecutively or in succession, as three wins one after another.

clue.text: Funny spin

definitions.meaning: a joke or witty remark, used as a noun
a short trip or outing, as a drive in the country

explanation.surface: An odd twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip is a witty remark, and the word also means a brief excursion or jaunt out of doors.

clue.text: Took off without reason, it's decided

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the word for took off goes around the other piece

parts.note: to ape someone is to imitate or mimic them, so took off is aped
the point of something is its purpose or reason

explanation.surface: Someone left without explanation, and that is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, in its old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A time or person that has been fixed or chosen in advance has been settled on, or determined.

clue.text: Come to wreck

definitions.meaning: to amount to, as a bill adding up to a sum
to write off or demolish, as a car smashed beyond repair

explanation.surface: Regaining consciousness amid a smashed-up scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill may amount to a sum, and informally a car smashed beyond repair has been written off completely.

clue.text: Queen and king on head of tossed coin, once

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of tossed is used

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714
R, from Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Describes the royal portraits stamped on an old coin flipped in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: A TANNER was the slang name for the old British sixpence, withdrawn after decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: This was everyday British slang for the sixpenny piece, a coin that ceased circulating after decimalisation.

clue.text: Shop requiring actual consignment

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods
very can mean actual or precise, as in 'the very man'

explanation.surface: A store needs the real shipment to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch of goods brought to a customer is a shipment, so the two words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Fury after game, seeing bloomer

indicators.note: the word for fury comes after the word for game

parts.note: snap is a card game where players call out matching cards
a dragon is a fierce, ferocious person, a fury

explanation.surface: Losing your temper over a game when you spot a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden plant has flowers that open like jaws when squeezed, so it is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: New name in development of earliest indoor sport

indicators.note: the two single letters are placed inside the rearranged word
a development reshapes something, so the letters of earliest are rearranged

explanation.surface: Novelty labels from the start of a game's evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' rearranges EARLIEST into REALTEIS, and 'in' puts NN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the original court game played indoors with a walled court, from which lawn tennis developed.

clue.text: Flower a daft male pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up reads the letters upwards, backwards

parts.note: daft means silly
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A foolish man yanked a bloom from the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' reverses SILLYRAM to MARYLLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This lily-like bulb with trumpet blooms is an example of a flower.

clue.text: Push skiver, finally, into school

indicators.note: the letter goes into the word for school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: only the last letter of skiver is used

explanation.surface: Shoving a truant back into the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is the whale sense: a group of whales or dolphins is a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke or nudge someone is a synonym of giving them a push.

clue.text: Doctor says one needs treatment for a period in the tropics

indicators.note: the letters are treated, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician says a patient needs treating for a spell abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs treatment' rearranges SAYS ONE into YSEASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical climates divide the year into wet and rainless halves, so this is one of those times.

clue.text: Northern stuff embraced by central US state

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the word for central

parts.note: key means central or crucial
to tuck in is to stuff yourself with food; tuck is also food

explanation.surface: Supplies from the north being welcomed in a state in the middle of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' looks like part of the definition but gives KEY, which surrounds N and TUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: This southern state, home of bourbon and the Derby, is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Pull one in custody back

indicators.note: the word for one in custody is read backwards

parts.note: a ward is a person, often a child, under the protection of a guardian or court

explanation.surface: Dragging a prisoner back to the cell.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul or tug something along is a synonym, as drawing a cart.

clue.text: A payment put into use, so I'm told

indicators.note: the letters are put inside the word for use

parts.note: to apply something is to use it
rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: Someone explains that money has been put to work, passing on what they heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegedly or reportedly, as a speaker says when passing on what others have said.

clue.text: Favourite partners, one doing a backflip, dancing together?

indicators.note: flipping backwards reverses the order of the letters

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as teacher's pet
in bridge, South and North are partners
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pair of favoured dancers, one performing an acrobatic flip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a backflip' reverses PETSNI; bridge pairs are North-South and East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancers moving in unison keep their feet in time, so this idiom for being in harmony fits.

clue.text: Perhaps beside a river, a vale to the East

parts.note: say can mean for example or perhaps
on can mean beside, as a town on a river

explanation.surface: A landscape description: maybe by a river, a valley in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vale' looks like a valley but is Latin for farewell; the answer is the Japanese goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Japanese word of parting, so it is goodbye, or vale, in the Far East.

clue.text: Funds raised for boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: pools are shared funds of money

explanation.surface: Money collected for buying a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-masted sailing vessel is an example of a boat.

clue.text: Main fix

definitions.meaning: chief or principal, as a basic foodstuff
to fasten with a bent metal wire clip

explanation.surface: Mending a main pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal commodity such as rice is the chief one, and a wire clip fastens papers together.

clue.text: Introduction to record in creative work — here?

definitions.text: Introduction to record in creative work — here?

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for creative work

parts.note: a poem is a piece of creative writing

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether a recording's preface belongs in an artistic piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a preface comes at the start of a written work.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a preface or preamble, the opening section at the start of a book or speech.

clue.text: Look at contracts for boss

indicators.note: something that contracts gets shorter, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to study something is to look at it closely

explanation.surface: Examining the agreements on behalf of the manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not the manager but a raised knob or ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ornamental knob on a surface is a nailhead or stud, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Young head-turner entering hotel, woman viewed from behind

indicators.note: the hidden letters are read backwards, from the end
the letters sit inside the words hotel and woman, running across them

explanation.surface: A striking young person walking into a hotel, seen from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' picks TELWO from hoTEL WOman, and 'viewed from behind' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls famously rotate their heads almost fully round, so a baby owl is a young head-turner.

clue.text: Socrates translated with guidance only beginning to be understood

indicators.note: just the first letter of guidance is used
translation changes the form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Greek philosophy rendered with a little help, finally making sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges SOCRATES plus G, the start of guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: When an idea is communicated successfully it comes over or registers with listeners, so it is grasped.

clue.text: After water flooded by effluent, initially put off

parts.note: post means after, as in postwar

indicators.note: the letter flows into the word for water

parts.note: a pond is a small body of water

indicators.note: only the first letter of effluent is used

explanation.surface: A pollution incident: the lake is swamped by waste and someone is repelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay or defer something to a later time is a synonym.

clue.text: Minions abandoning southern nation

indicators.note: the letter for southern is left out of the word for minions

parts.note: yes-men are sycophantic followers who always agree

explanation.surface: Followers deserting a southern country.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arab country on the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula is an example of a nation.
